caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: DANDI:001676
attempts.entry_title: Months-long stability of the head-direction system (Skromne Carrasco et al. 2026)
attempts.summary: Most central findings held in this data: head-direction tuning stayed stable across weeks, offsets between cell pairs were preserved, and drift rates matched the paper. Remapping between environments held in part: the offsets and an environment classifier reproduced, but coherent remapping did not (10 of 15 mouse and environment pairs against the 80% sought). That result depends on how head-direction cells are defined, which the paper does not fully state. The probe-week memory findings could not be tested because no table links cells across the two protocols, and decoding across days exceeded the runner's time limit. Single-visit memory held in part, and the per-session proportions of head-direction cells did not reproduce.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Skromne Carrasco, Viejo and Peyrache (2026) on dandiset 001676, which holds 402 Miniscope sessions of postsubiculum HD cells in ten mice over four protocols and one silicon probe session in each of four mice. It tests the stability of preferred directions and pairwise offsets over four weeks and across four environments, the environment code, remapping between environments, memory after a single visit, and the electrophysiology offsets. The probe trials of Fig. 3 cannot be linked to earlier sessions, and the spike waveforms are not in the files.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Skromne Carrasco et al. (2026) from dandiset 001676
Head-direction decoders of Skromne Carrasco et al. (2026) on dandiset 001676

outcomes.statement: Across 388 imaging sessions, the number of ROIs per session ranged from 21 to 286 (95 plus or minus 56, mean and s.d.), and was stable over time.
outcomes.source: Results, The tuning of HD cells is stable over time, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 1d
outcomes.quote: Across a total of 388 sessions, the number of ROIs per session ranged from 21 to 286 (95 ± 56 (mean ± s.d.)) and was stable over time
outcomes.notes: The dataset holds 402 imaging sessions over all ten mice and 367 for mice 1 to 5, and neither is the paper's 388 (tolerance 0). ROIs per session range from 22 to 291, mean 102.1, s.d. 60.6 (reading a), or 26 to 286, mean 98.9, s.d. 56.7 (reading b); both are within tolerance. ROI count against session number in the circular protocol has a Spearman p below 0.05 in 2 of 5 mice (mouse 3 rho -0.87, mouse 4 rho 0.63), so a majority show no trend.
deviations: The "stable over time" test (Spearman per mouse, majority not significant) is the reader's; the paper gives no test.

outcomes.statement: In the four-week circular protocol, the median proportion of ROIs detected as HD cells per animal was 0.2, 0.7, 0.4, 0.7 and 0.2, with 72, 42, 197, 48 and 102 ROIs per session on average, over 19, 20, 19, 19 and 20 recordings.
outcomes.source: Extended Data Fig. 1e legend
outcomes.quote: Median proportion ± s.d. per animal = 0.2 ± 0.03, 0.7 ± 0.04, 0.4 ± 0.05, 0.7 ± 0.05, 0.2 ± 0.04. n = 19, 20, 19, 19, 20 recordings per animal, with a respective mean ± s.d. of ROIs detected 72 ± 16, 42 ± 5, 197 ± 18, 48 ± 12, 102 ± 25
outcomes.notes: Recording counts match exactly (19, 20, 19, 19, 20). Mean ROIs per session are within the stated s.d. for mice 1, 2 and 4 and above it for mice 3 (238.8 against 197 +- 18) and 5 (129.8 against 102 +- 25). Under all four HD rule readings (kernel 12 degrees or 12 bins, HDI on the raw or smoothed curve) and both counting readings, at most 1 of 5 median proportions is within tolerance. Measured values are the main reading (12 degree kernel, smoothed HDI) with reading (a); raw HDI gives 0.256, 0.641, 0.099, 0.477, 0.209 (a) and 0.333, 0.879, 0.559, 0.810, 0.440 (b). The paper's proportions do not follow from its own HD rule on these data under any reading tried.
deviations: The HDI formula for dF/F, the kernel and whether HDI uses the smoothed curve are not stated; all four combinations are shown.

outcomes.statement: An Isomap projection of the HD cell population activity forms a ring, reflecting the circular representation of head direction.
outcomes.source: Results, The tuning of HD cells is stable over time, paragraph 2; Extended Data Fig. 1h
outcomes.quote: Low-dimensional projection of HD cell population activity using Isomap (Methods), a technique for... high-dimensional data by preserving its geometric structure, revealed a ring topology
outcomes.notes: With z-scored activity the angle around the Isomap embedding is correlated with head direction in all five example sessions (circular-circular correlation, |r| 0.19 to 0.81, p below 0.05; 1222 to 1300 bins, 32 to 82 cells). With division by the maximum, 4 of 5 sessions keep fewer than 51 bins above the 0.1 threshold, too few for 50 neighbours; the fifth gives r -0.63. Mouse 1's ring is weak (r -0.19). The p values treat the 0.25 s bins as independent, which they are not, so they overstate the evidence.
deviations: The test and its counts are the claims file's, not the paper's (which judges the ring by eye).
The example session per mouse is the one with the most ROIs whose split-half correlation exceeds 0.8, a standard choice; the paper does not name its sessions.
Normalization is read as z-scoring (assumption); division by the maximum leaves too few bins with the paper's 0.1 threshold.
Cells are chosen with HDI on the smoothed curve only; raw HDI was not run for this claim.

outcomes.statement: In an example mouse, the population change in preferred direction relative to the last session was concentrated around 0 degrees (V-test, v = 17.06, P < 0.001, 18 sessions, median absolute deviation 5.0 degrees).
outcomes.source: Fig. 1f legend; Results, The tuning of HD cells is stable over time, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Population average of across-session angular difference in preferred direction, relative to the last session for one example mouse (V-test, not different from 0°, v = 17.06, two-tailed P < 0.001, n = 18 sessions, median absolute deviation from 0° = 5.0°)
outcomes.notes: Under the main reading, mouse 2 has 18 compared sessions, V 17.01, median absolute deviation 4.6 degrees and two-sided p below 0.001 (reading b). Mouse 4, which Extended Data Fig. 1g names as the animal of Fig. 1 (reading a), gives V 14.29 and 7.2 degrees, outside tolerance. With raw HDI no mouse with 18 compared sessions matches (mouse 2 then has 19, V 18.35, 5.3 degrees). The V of mouse 2 also matches the second value of Extended Data Fig. 4b (17.1), so the Fig. 1 example appears to be mouse 2.
deviations: Assumed HDI on the smoothed tuning curve with the 12 degree kernel, as the main reading for every HD cell claim. The stored tuning curves of the files match a 4-bin (12 degree) kernel, and smoothed HDI gives the paper's numbers of compared sessions (18 here; 84 pooled in Fig. 1g against 85 here; 16, 18, 16, 16 in Extended Data Fig. 4a against 16, 18, 16, 17) and of offset values (25,901 against 25,441), where raw HDI gives 92 sessions and 92,537 values.
Detected in at least six sessions is read as registered by CellReg in at least six sessions, and the average HDI is over the registered sessions that pass the split-half rule.

outcomes.statement: Across all five mice, the population change in preferred direction relative to the last session was concentrated around 0 degrees (V-test, v = 75.21, P < 0.001, 84 sessions), with per-mouse means of 15.4, 2.1, -5.5, -7.8 and -6.9 degrees.
outcomes.source: Fig. 1g legend
outcomes.quote: Distribution of population-wise angular difference relative to the last session for all five mice (V-test, not different from 0°, v = 75.21, two-tailed P < 0.001, n = 84 sessions). Per mouse... 15.4 ± 24.7°, 2.1 ± 18.7°, −5.5 ± 15.2°, −7.8 ± 23.6°, −6.9 ± 41.5° (mean ± s.d.)
outcomes.notes: Pooled V 75.58 over 85 sessions (paper 75.21 over 84), one-sided p below 0.001. All five per-mouse circular means are within the paper's s.d. Under the other three readings the pooled V is 62.4 to 80.0, all means hold, and the session count is 75 to 92. The 85 against 84 sessions is outside the count's tolerance of 0; the criterion does not use the count. The five means have the paper's sign; with the sign reversed 4 of 5 are within tolerance and none has the paper's sign, so the outcome does not depend on the sign.
deviations: Main HD reading as for fig1f-example-stable (assumption).

outcomes.statement: The V statistic of the change in preferred direction relative to the last session was 14.1, 17.1, 17.3, 14.6 and 12.2 per animal, against shuffle medians of 3.0, 3.2, 5.7, 4.8 and 2.0, and 75.2 pooled against a shuffle median of 18.6; each animal's distribution was concentrated around 0 degrees (P < 0.001).
outcomes.source: Extended Data Fig. 4a,b legends
outcomes.quote: V statistic per animal = 14.1, 17.1, 17.3, 14.6, 12.2. Median of V statistic shuffles per animal = 3.0, 3.2, 5.7, 4.8, 2.0. Left... V-test statistic for pooled animals (75.2) versus the distribution of V statistic for within-day shuffled cell identity (median = 18.6)
outcomes.notes: All five V are within 10% of the paper's and each exceeds its shuffle median (2.63, 6.46, 11.94, 7.12, 2.58 against the paper's 3.0, 3.2, 5.7, 4.8, 2.0). The pooled shuffle median is 30.8 against 18.6, outside its tolerance; the criterion does not use it. With raw HDI, 4 of 5 V are within tolerance and the pooled shuffle median is 16.5. One-sided p per mouse 6.5e-09 to 2.4e-06.
deviations: Main HD reading as for fig1f-example-stable (assumption).
The shuffle permutes cell identity in the compared session; the V-test is pycircstat's formula, reimplemented (pycircstat does not import under numpy 2).

outcomes.statement: The change in preferred direction relative to the previous session was also concentrated around 0 degrees across the five animals (V-test, P < 0.001, 75 sessions; pooled V 69.9 against a shuffle median of 21.9).
outcomes.source: Extended Data Fig. 4c,d legends
outcomes.quote: Distribution of population- wise angular difference relative to the previous session for all five animals (V-test, not different from 0°, two-tailed p < 0.001, n = 75 sessions)
outcomes.notes: Pooled V 70.00 over 78 sessions (paper 69.9 over 75), one-sided p below 0.001; per-animal V within tolerance in 4 of 5 (mouse 5 12.71 against 10.1 +- 1.01). The pooled shuffle median 26.6 is outside 21.9 +- 2.19. Under raw HDI the pooled V is 80.0 (outside) and only 1 of 5 per-animal V is within, so the outcome rests on the HDI reading.
deviations: Main HD reading as for fig1f-example-stable (assumption).

outcomes.statement: The Jaccard index of HD cell detection between sessions of the circular protocol remained high regardless of the delay between sessions.
outcomes.source: Results, The tuning of HD cells is stable over time, paragraph 2; Extended Data Fig. 2a,b
outcomes.quote: The Jaccard index remained high regardless of... the delay between sessions, suggesting that most ROIs were... registered and continued to exhibit activity across time
outcomes.notes: Under the main reading, the median Jaccard index at the longest interval (23 to 25 days) is at least 80% of the one-day value in 2 of 5 mice with reading (a) (ratios 0.74, 0.97, 1.43, 0.65, 0.00) and in 3 of 5 with reading (b), where mice 4 and 5 have 1 and 3 ROIs registered in every session and give no value. With raw HDI, reading (a) holds in 5 of 5 (ratios 0.92 to 1.29).
deviations: Main HD reading as for fig1f-example-stable (assumption); the outcome changes with it.
The 80% threshold is the reader's.

outcomes.statement: The shift in preferred direction between the first and last recording was not significantly related to the displacement of the ROI centroid in the field of view (p = 0.290) or to the CellReg score (p = 0.344), while centroid displacement was related to CellReg score (p = 0.004).
outcomes.source: Results, The tuning of HD cells is stable over time, paragraph 3; Extended Data Fig. 2c-e
outcomes.quote: the change in preferred direction was not significantly correlated with the quality of cell registration nor the drift of the ROI in the Miniscope field of view

statistics.about: shift in preferred direction against centroid displacement, all cells
same, cells with CellReg score over 0.8
CellReg score against shift in preferred direction

outcomes.notes: Over all cells, with every valid CellReg score (the paper's "all cells"), 49 HD cells are valid in the first and last session under the main reading and 106 with raw HDI (paper 72); two raw-HDI cells with a CellReg score below 0 (-0.096, -0.01) are dropped. Pooled over mice, shift against displacement has p 0.074 (signed) and 0.62 (absolute), shift against score p 0.98 and 0.38, both not significant, and displacement against score p 0.0003 (slope -34.4 um per unit score), 0.0011 after Bonferroni over the figure's 4 tests. With raw HDI the absence tests give p 0.084 to 0.24 and displacement against score p below 0.0001. For mouse 4 alone (10 or 19 cells) displacement against score is not significant (p 0.96 and 0.94), so reading (b) fails. Restricted to cells with score above 0.8 (28 or 56 cells, the analysis before verification), displacement against score is 0.67 and 0.055 after Bonferroni over 4, so under that reading of "all cells" the claim would not reproduce; the outcome rests on the all-scores reading. Changed from not reproduced after verification.
deviations: Main HD reading as for fig1f-example-stable; raw HDI gives the same outcome.

All cells are taken as HD cells with any valid CellReg score (0 or above; scores below 0 are not CellReg confidence scores and are dropped), since the paper tests "all cells" and, separately, "cells with CellReg score over 0.8" (Extended Data Fig. 2 legend, as the claims file lists the statistics). Bonferroni over the four tests of the claims file.
Centroids are mask-weighted centres of the image masks, at 3.3 um per pixel (grid_spacing); the paper does not say how displacement was measured.

outcomes.statement: The absolute change in preferred direction grew slowly with the days between recordings, at a drift rate of 7.1 plus or minus 4.4 degrees per week across mice.
outcomes.source: Results, The tuning of HD cells is stable over time, paragraph 3; Fig. 1h
outcomes.quote: we computed the absolute change in preferred direction as a function of days passed between recordings and observed... a slow drift rate (7.1 ± 4.4° per week)
outcomes.notes: Mean drift 6.71 degrees per week over mice (per mouse 6.2, -1.2, 4.3, 14.0, 10.3) with value reading (a) and drift reading (a); value reading (b) gives 7.47. Drift readings a and b are within 7.1 +- 4.4 under all four HD readings (6.06 to 9.03); reading c (line through the origin) gives 13.0 to 17.7.
deviations: The drift rate is not defined in the paper; it is taken as the least-squares slope of the absolute change against day difference times 7 (reading a), an assumption; the other readings are shown.

outcomes.statement: The drift in preferred direction was not diffusive (not a random walk) but fluctuated around a fixed direction, as shown by the cumulative variance of orientation across days.
outcomes.source: Results, The tuning of HD cells is stable over time, paragraph 3; Extended Data Fig. 4e,f
outcomes.quote: Analysis of the cumulative variance of orientation across days suggested that this drift, although modest, was not diffusive (that is, not a random walk) but instead... around a fixed direction
outcomes.notes: With changes relative to the last day (reading a), the variance over all recordings is below half the value of a line through the origin fitted to the first five points in 4 of 5 mice (mouse 2, 421 against 127, is the exception). Relative to the first day (reading b) it holds in 2 of 5. Under raw HDI reading (a) holds in 3 of 5. The readings differ only in the reference session and in which cells enter each session's change, so the pass rests on noisy session values and is fragile.
deviations: The test and its threshold are the reader's; the paper shows the curve without a test.
Main HD reading as for fig1f-example-stable (assumption).

outcomes.statement: The absolute change in overall preferred direction with respect to the last day was smaller than for shuffled cell identities in every animal (median 15.9, 5.1, 7.9, 26.3 and 24.0 degrees; one-tailed Wilcoxon, p from 3.8e-6 to 1.5e-4).
outcomes.source: Extended Data Fig. 4f legend
outcomes.quote: Absolute change in overall preferred direction, per session, with respect to the last day of the experiment in Fig. 1. Median absolute change per animal in degrees... 15.9, 5.1, 7.9, 26.3, 24.0
outcomes.notes: Under the main reading 3 of 5 medians are within 10%, but the one-tailed Wilcoxon is not significant for mouse 3 (W 30, p 0.079 with the median shuffle; W 38, p 0.106 with the mean). Under raw HDI all five tests are significant (p at most 0.001) but only 2 of 5 medians are within 10% (12.7, 5.3, 6.4, 6.4, 25.7). No reading meets both parts. The effect is present, significant in 4 of 5 mice under the main reading and in 5 of 5 with raw HDI, so the outcome is partially reproduced (changed from not reproduced after verification).

outcomes.statement: The change in pairwise angular offset across all registered HD cell pairs was strongly biased towards 0, with per-animal medians of 12, 9, 12, 24 and 12 degrees against shuffle medians of 51 to 54 degrees (p < 0.001 per animal, 25,901 pairs).
outcomes.source: Results, The tuning of HD cells is stable over time, paragraph 4; Extended Data Fig. 4g
outcomes.quote: The change in pairwise angular offset across all registered cell pairs (... of interleaving days) was strongly biased towards 0 (Extended Data Fig. 4g), suggesting highly coherent population dynamics
outcomes.notes: Unsigned offsets, main HD reading; medians 12, 9, 12, 21, 12 degrees, each below all 1,000 shuffled medians (shuffle medians 48, 51, 39, 51, 51; paper 51 to 54). 1,506 cell pairs and 25,441 cell pair by session pair values (paper 25,901 pairs). Signed offsets give medians 12, 9, 15, 33, 12, also within tolerance and below all shuffles, with shuffle medians 72 to 90. Raw HDI gives medians 15 to 30, all within tolerance and below all shuffles.
deviations: The paper's shuffle medians (51 to 54 degrees) are what unsigned offsets (0 to 180 degrees) give, 180 (1 - 1/sqrt 2) = 52.7 for independent offsets, while signed offsets give 90. Unsigned offsets are the main reading for the offset claims (assumption); both are shown here and agree.
The shuffled medians are read from 3 degree histograms of the shuffled changes; the changes are multiples of 3 degrees, so this is exact up to ties.

outcomes.statement: The change in pairwise angular offset drifted more slowly (4.1 plus or minus 4.8 degrees per week) than single cell tuning, though not significantly so.
outcomes.source: Results, The tuning of HD cells is stable over time, paragraph 4; Fig. 1i
outcomes.quote: the change in pairwise angular offset drifted more slowly (4.1 ± 4.8° per week), yet this was not significantly different from single cell tuning drift rate
outcomes.notes: Offset drift 5.32 degrees per week (reading a; s.d. 4.62; per mouse 4.91, -0.11, 1.45, 12.92, 7.43), within 4.1 +- 4.8; reading b 5.41, reading c 12.17. Against the preferred direction drift (mean 6.71) the two-sided Wilcoxon gives W 2, p 0.188, and the paired t-test t -1.89, p 0.132, mean difference -1.39 degrees per week; neither is significant under any drift reading. With raw HDI the offset drift is 5.46 (Wilcoxon p 0.625).
deviations: Unsigned offsets (assumption, see edf4g) and the drift rate as a least-squares slope (assumption, see fig1h).

outcomes.statement: Decoders of head direction trained on one session and tested on another decoded significantly better than chance for nearly the whole four weeks of the experiment.
outcomes.source: Results, The tuning of HD cells is stable over time, paragraph 5; Fig. 1j,k
outcomes.quote: we trained and tested non-linear decoders (extreme gradient-boosted trees (Methods)) on every recording session pair and observed statistically significant decoding for nearly the entire duration of the experiment
outcomes.notes: The claim's decoders run on every ordered pair of the 97 circular sessions plus each session split in halves, 1,883 XGBoost fits (1,189 for the pairs up to 10 days apart of the partial reading). The 507 fits of decoding.ipynb, four at a time on the same decoder (the runner has four cores), take 2.56 s each, an estimate of 80 minutes of fits for all pairs and 51 minutes up to 10 days, plus loading the 97 circular sessions (the 227 sessions of decoding.ipynb took 1125 s), against the 60 minute limit of a notebook. Nothing of the claim was run. The data it needs are in the dataset.

outcomes.statement: The population vector coherence decayed slowly over the course of the recording.
outcomes.source: Results, The tuning of HD cells is stable over time, paragraph 5; Extended Data Fig. 4h-j
outcomes.quote: This is in line with a slow decay in the population vector coherence over the course of the recording
outcomes.notes: Under both readings the population vector correlation decreases with day difference in 4 of 5 mice (Spearman rho -0.58, -0.19, -0.55, -0.87 with p below 0.02; mouse 5 rho -0.15, p 0.11, reading a), and its mean at the longest difference stays above 0 (0.09 to 0.86). With raw HDI it decreases in 5 of 5 under both readings, and the mean at the longest difference of mouse 5 is -0.00 (a) and -0.19 (b), so the outcome rests on the main HD reading.
deviations: Main HD reading as for fig1f-example-stable (assumption); with raw HDI the mean at the longest difference is above 0 in 4 of 5 mice.
Population vectors use the raw tuning curves of HD cells valid in both sessions, averaged into 12 bins; the paper does not give the cells or the smoothing.

outcomes.statement: Across the four environments, HD cells preserved their pairwise angular offsets, with per-animal median changes of 24, 12, 18, 29 and 12 degrees against shuffle medians of 54 to 57 degrees, and a drift rate of 1.9 plus or minus 1.02 degrees per week.
outcomes.source: Results, Internal organization across time and environments, paragraph 1; Fig. 2e; Extended Data Fig. 6b
outcomes.quote: We observed the same tendency of preserved pairwise angular difference in preferred directions across... all sessions and mice (Fig. 2e and Extended Data Fig. 6)
outcomes.notes: Unsigned offsets; medians 24, 9, 15, 27, 12 degrees, all within the paper's s.d. and each below all 1,000 shuffled medians (51 to 57). Mean drift (reading a) 2.41 degrees per week with mouse 2 excluded and 2.28 included; reading b 2.00 and 1.79; all within 1.9 +- 1.02. Reading c gives 6.9 (outside). Signed offsets also put the medians within tolerance but give mean drift 3.4 to 6.0 (outside), and raw HDI gives 1.2 to 2.2 (within).
deviations: Unsigned offsets (assumption, see edf4g) and the drift rate as a least-squares slope (assumption, see fig1h). With signed offsets the drift is outside tolerance.

outcomes.statement: The tuning of HD cells was stable within each environment, with changes in preferred direction relative to the last day concentrated around 0 degrees in all four, and no difference between environments (repeated-measures ANOVA, F = 0.44, P = 0.73).
outcomes.source: Results, Internal organization across time and environments, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 5c
outcomes.quote: The tuning of HD cells was stable within each environment for all mice
outcomes.notes: V over 45, 39, 44 and 43 sessions (the paper's n), all p below 0.001; 3 of 4 within 10% (square 13.81 against 15.5 +- 1.55 is not). Repeated-measures ANOVA over environments with mice as subjects, F 1.01, df 3/12, p 0.42 (mean absolute change) and F 0.84, p 0.50 (median); not significant. Raw HDI gives V 44.01, 16.30, 34.02, 31.44 (4 of 4 within) and ANOVA p 0.46 and 0.51.

outcomes.statement: Electrophysiological recordings confirmed that pairwise angular offsets of HD cells are preserved across environments, with per-animal median changes of 18, 12, 27 and 15 degrees against shuffle medians of 54 degrees (p < 0.001).
outcomes.source: Results, Internal organization across time and environments, paragraph 2; Extended Data Fig. 7e
outcomes.quote: To confirm that this long-tailed distribution is not specific to the imaging... we confirmed these results with electrophysiological recordings
outcomes.notes: Unsigned offsets over the first exploration of each environment; medians 6, 6, 9, 6 degrees, within the paper's s.d., each below all 1,000 shuffled medians (51 to 57). Signed offsets and all six explorations give the same outcome (medians 6 to 15). The four files hold 254 PoSub units, the paper's n of 254 cells; 99 are HD cells with HDI on the smoothed curve and 118 with raw HDI, against 125 +- 12.5. With the 118 raw-HDI cells the medians are 6, 9, 9, 6, also below all shuffles, under both offset readings and both exploration readings. The medians are lower than the paper's 12 to 27.
deviations: Each file holds two explorations of each environment separated by sleep; the paper describes one. The first explorations are the main reading.
Spike tuning curves use the imaging bins and kernel (the claims file's reading); rate and HDI are averaged over the three first explorations, a standard choice.
Units are those on shanks whose electrode group is located in PSB; the files also hold cortex and CA1 units.

outcomes.statement: Electrophysiologically recorded HD cells have broader waveforms than non-HD cells (median trough-to-peak 0.54 against 0.295 ms, half-peak width 0.21 against 0.165 ms).
outcomes.source: Extended Data Fig. 7g legend
outcomes.quote: Note HD cells tend to have broader waveforms, consistent with pyramidal cells. Median HD trough-to-peak = 0.54 ms, median HD half-peak width = 0.21 ms, versus 0.295 and 0.165 respectively for non-HD cells; n = 254 cells
outcomes.notes: The electrophysiology files hold spike times and electrode groups per unit, with no waveforms, waveform means, raw voltage or channel per unit (units table columns are spike_times and electrode_group only). The waveform features cannot be computed. Checked on the four ecephys files of the pinned version.

outcomes.statement: For recordings 7 days apart, decoders trained and tested in the same environment tended to be better than across environments, and the change in pairwise offset tended to be smaller, neither significantly (p = 0.063 for both).
outcomes.source: Results, Environmental modulation of the HD cell population, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 8b,c
outcomes.quote: Decoders of head direction of mice trained and tested in the same environment one week apart showed a tendency for better (yet non-significant) accuracy than decoders trained across environments with the same delay between sessions

statistics.about: change in angular offset, single against mixed
decoder error variance, single against mixed

outcomes.notes: 159 pairs 7 days apart (92 single, 67 mixed). Offset change, single 15.2 against mixed 19.5 degrees, both within the paper's means; single lower in 4 of 5 mice, W 1, p 0.125. Decoder error, circular variance single 0.53 against mixed 0.65, both within tolerance; lower in 4 of 5, W 1, p 0.125. Linear variance of the signed error, single 1.91 against 3.15 radians squared; lower in 5 of 5, W 0, p 0.062 as in the paper, but far from the paper's 0.58 and 0.74. The tendency is present and not significant, as the paper says, but no reading gives W 0 with means within tolerance. Mixed decoders are at chance (median error 80 to 109 against chance 86 to 91 degrees). With raw HDI the offset change matches fully (single 19.6 against mixed 27.1 degrees, within tolerance, lower in 5 of 5, W 0, p 0.062), but the decoder does not (circular variance 0.51 against 0.64, lower in 4 of 5, p 0.125; linear variance lower in 5 of 5 with values far from the paper's). With test cells required only to be registered in the test session, the results are those of the main reading (circular variance 0.53 against 0.66, 4 of 5).
deviations: The decoder cell rule (HD cells meeting the score, split-half and HDI rule in both sessions), normalization by each cell's maximum and population activity as the sum of normalized activity are assumptions; XGBoost uses library defaults. The rule loosened in the test session and raw HDI are shown.
Unsigned offsets (assumption, see edf4g).

outcomes.statement: Classifiers of environment identity trained on pairwise correlations of HD cell tuning curves were more accurate than shuffles (proportion correct 0.7 against 0.3; one-sided Wilcoxon, P = 0.031, W = 15).
outcomes.source: Results, Environmental modulation of the HD cell population, paragraph 1; Fig. 2f,g
outcomes.quote: These classifiers showed higher accuracy than controls (Fig. 2f,g)... the idea that the HD signal in the PoSub is environment specific
outcomes.notes: Mean over 100 random splits 0.64 (s.d. 0.04 over mice) against 0.28 for shuffles, one-sided Wilcoxon W 15, p 0.031; a single split gives 0.70 against 0.21, same test. Chance with four environments is 0.25. Features per mouse 496 to 2,775 pairs, 11 to 23% of them finite. With raw HDI 0.59 against 0.26 (single split 0.63 against 0.28), W 15, p 0.031. The criterion is met, but the controls do not show that the classifier reads the correlations. Given only which cell pairs are present in a recording (features set to 1 where present), it reaches 0.70 against 0.28. Trained and tested on different halves of each environment's two-week block, it reaches 0.48 against 0.27 (W 15, p 0.031). With the correlations permuted among the pairs present in each recording (presence pattern kept), it reaches 0.59 against 0.64 for the data (lower in 5 of 5 mice, W 15, p 0.031), so the correlations add a little to the presence pattern.
deviations: Cell pairs not both valid in a recording enter as missing values, which XGBoost handles; the paper does not say how absent cells enter (assumption).

outcomes.statement: The remapping of the HD system between the three environments of one room seemed random across mice (Rayleigh test, P = 0.36 circular to square, 0.61 square to radial maze, 0.032 radial maze to circular).
outcomes.source: Results, Environmental modulation of the HD cell population, paragraph 2; Fig. 2h,i
outcomes.quote: Notably, this remapping seemed random across mice, although more data would be required to support a true random remapping
outcomes.notes: Rayleigh z 1.28 (p 0.29) circular to square, 0.70 (p 0.52) square to 8-arm maze, 2.58 (p 0.069) 8-arm maze to circular. The first two are not significant as in the paper; the third is not significant where the paper reports p 0.032, and no z is within 10%. Raw HDI gives z 1.31 (p 0.28), 0.45 (p 0.66) and 2.66 (p 0.063), the same outcome. Mouse 2 has 2 recording pairs with cells in common for 8-arm maze to circular, across its Miniscope change.

outcomes.statement: While the internal structure of the HD system was largely kept across environments, its absolute orientation was specific to each environment, the HD cells of a mouse shifting together (coherent remapping) compared with shuffled cell identities.
outcomes.source: Results, Environmental modulation of the HD cell population, paragraph 2; Fig. 2c,d,h,i
outcomes.quote: Whereas the internal structure of the HD system was largely preserved across environments, with only minor... its absolute orientation was specific to each environment
outcomes.notes: Coherent (median mean vector length over recording pairs above the median shuffle 95th percentile) in 10 of 15 mouse and environment pairs, 67% against the criterion's 80%. The five failures are mouse 2 (8-arm maze to circular, 0.33 against 0.98 over 2 recording pairs; square to 8-arm maze, 0.13 against 0.39 over 11, both across its Miniscope change), mouse 3 (8-arm maze to circular, 0.76 against 0.79; square to 8-arm maze, 0.93 against 0.95) and mouse 4 (8-arm maze to circular, 0.36 against 0.55). The absolute average remapping exceeds 30 degrees in 3 to 5 mice for every pair. With the open field pairs (variant), 11 of 14 are coherent. With raw HDI, which keeps about twice as many cells per recording pair, 12 of 15 are coherent (80%, at the threshold; mouse 3's two failures pass), with remapping above 30 degrees in at least 3 mice for every pair, which meets the criterion. The outcome rests on the HDI reading.
deviations: The 80% and 30 degree thresholds are the reader's.
Main HD reading as for fig1f-example-stable (assumption); the outcome changes with it.

outcomes.statement: After a delay without visits, the orientation of the HD system in each environment was retained, drifting slowly with the delay; it was concentrated around 0 degrees for delays under 1, 2 and 4 weeks (V-test, P = 0.002, 0.02, 0.03) but not at 6 weeks (P = 0.191), with mean absolute changes of 3.6, 23.9, 39.6 and 70.0 degrees.
outcomes.source: Results, HD system forms long-term memories of orientation, paragraph 1; Fig. 3d
outcomes.quote: the average alignment of the HD system to external environments across mice drifted gradually, albeit slowly, as the interval between sessions increased, becoming significantly... from 0° only at the 6-week delay
outcomes.notes: The probe week is in the dataset, as the first week of the protocol "4 environments are visited weekly in a random order, for 4 weeks" (one session per environment on the four days after the last day of the two-week protocol). Each protocol has its own CellReg table, with one column per session of that protocol only, and no table or identifier links ROIs of the two-week protocol to those of the probe week. The remapping between the last visit and the probe trial needs the same cells in both, so it cannot be computed. Checked in every file's scratch tables and in the dandiset metadata.

outcomes.statement: The mean vector length of the remapping angles across mice decreased with delay (0.998, 0.79, 0.79 and 0.536 for under 1, 2, 4 and 6 weeks), compared with shuffled HD cell identities.
outcomes.source: Fig. 3d (the mvl values printed in the panel) and Fig. 3e
outcomes.quote: Mean vector length of animal remapping angles (that is, probe versus last visit of each environment, for n = 4 mice) as a function of delay between visits compared to controls (shuffled HD cell identity)
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig3de-probe-memory, blocked for lack of a registration across protocols.

outcomes.statement: The absolute change in individual preferred directions drifted with delay at 10.8 plus or minus 0.1 degrees per week, while the pairwise angular offsets stayed coherent, drifting at 2.5 plus or minus 0.1 degrees per week.
outcomes.source: Results, HD system forms long-term memories of orientation, paragraph 1; Fig. 3f,g
outcomes.quote: We further tested this drift by assessing the absolute changes in individual neuronal preferred directions and observed a similar drift from the original direction (Fig. 3f). Of note, the population structure maintained its coherence across these recordings
outcomes.notes: Needs per-cell and per-pair changes between the last visit of the two-week protocol and the probe trial, which need the cell registration across protocols that the dataset does not hold (see fig3de-probe-memory).

outcomes.statement: After four further weeks of visits to the four environments in random order, the system showed reduced retention of the original preferred direction, though changes relative to week 1 stayed centred on 0 degrees (V = 11.3, 10.1, 10.8), and pairwise offsets drifted at a mean of 1.6 degrees per week.
outcomes.source: Results, HD system forms long-term memories of orientation, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 9b,d
outcomes.quote: this orientation memory may be affected by cognitive load as after four additional weeks of extensive experience with the different... the systems showed reduced retention of the original preferred direction
outcomes.notes: V 10.38, 8.91 and 10.56 over 19, 19 and 18 values (paper 20, 20, 18), all with p below 0.01; week 3 is outside 10.1 +- 1.01. The pairwise offset drift is 0.68 degrees per week (reading a; b -0.11, c 11.70) against 1.6 +- 0.16; per mouse 0.83, 1.25, 3.31, -0.87, -1.14. With six sessions required, the same (V 10.38, 8.57, 10.48; drift 0.61). With raw HDI, V 10.24, 8.68, 10.71 and drift -0.52. The reduced-retention comparison needs the 4-week probe value of fig3de-probe-memory, which is blocked; the mean absolute change at week 4 relative to week 1 is 42.2 degrees. Changes relative to week 1 stay centred on 0 (all V-tests significant), but the drift rate and one V are outside tolerance, and the retention part cannot be tested, so the claim holds in part (changed from not reproduced after verification). The probe week is identified from the dates printed in the notebook; the random protocol starts 3 days after the last two-week session for mice 1 to 4 and 81 days after it for mouse 5.
deviations: The minimum number of sessions for this figure is not stated; two (as for Fig. 3, the same protocol) is the main reading and six is shown; they agree.
Weeks are 7-day blocks from the protocol's first session; week 1 is the probe week.
Unsigned offsets (assumption, see edf4g).

outcomes.statement: After a single visit, the orientation of the HD cell population was retained four weeks later as well as with weekly visits; the change in preferred direction from first to last session was smaller than shuffles in both groups (one-sided Wilcoxon, P = 0.031) and did not differ between groups (P = 0.438; weekly 12.4, single 6.6 degrees).
outcomes.source: Results, Memory from a single visit is stable over weeks, paragraph 1; Fig. 4d
outcomes.quote: We observed a highly maintained absolute orientation of the HD cell... for both environments
outcomes.notes: In both groups the change is smaller than shuffles (one-sided Wilcoxon W 0, p 0.031, with the median or the mean shuffle) and the groups do not differ (two-sided W 2, p 0.188). The weekly mean 6.2 degrees is within 12.4 +- 10.0; the single mean 21.9 (s.d. 16.0) is outside 6.6 +- 4.1, raised by mouse 8 (48 degrees from 2 cells) and mouse 10 (30 degrees from 9 cells). With raw HDI the tests are the same (W 0, p 0.031 in both groups; group test W 4, p 0.438, the paper's values), the weekly mean is 8.3 (within) and the single mean 12.4 (outside). Under both readings both means would fit if the groups were swapped.

outcomes.statement: A decoder of head direction trained on the first and tested on the last session was accurate for both environments, with no difference between the weekly and single groups (weekly 35.9, single 43.9 degrees median error; P = 0.438).
outcomes.source: Results, Memory from a single visit is stable over weeks, paragraph 1; Fig. 4e
outcomes.quote: This was further supported by the high accuracy of a decoder of head direction for both environments (not significantly different from other animals)
outcomes.notes: Mean median error weekly 42.5 degrees (s.d. 20.3) and single 48.8 (s.d. 18.5), within tolerance; every decoder is below its time-reversed chance (83 to 97 degrees); weekly against single, two-sided Wilcoxon W 3, p 0.312. Mouse 8 decodes from 4 and 2 cells (errors 78 and 85). Raw HDI (41.7 and 48.1, W 4, p 0.438) and test cells required only to be registered in the test session (44.0 and 49.4, W 4, p 0.438) give the same outcome, with every decoder below chance.
deviations: Decoder assumptions as for edf8-same-vs-mixed.

outcomes.statement: The change in preferred direction from first to last visit did not differ between the two environments (circular mean 1.6 against 5.1 degrees; two-sided Wilcoxon, p = 1.0, n = 10).
outcomes.source: Extended Data Fig. 10c legend
outcomes.quote: Change in preferred direction first versus last visit, classified by environment identity. Circular mean ± s.d. in degrees... 1.6 ± 14.1, 5.1 ± 8.0. Two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank p = 1.0, W statistic = 7.0, n = 10

statistics.n: 10 values, read as 5 mice by 2 environments

outcomes.notes: The two-sided Wilcoxon paired by mouse is not significant (W 3, p 0.312), as in the paper. With the change taken as the first visit minus the later one (main sign reading), circular means are -0.2 degrees (circular, s.d. 15.1) and 12.8 (square, s.d. 19.5), within tolerance under either assignment. With the opposite sign (later minus first, the sign before verification) square is -12.8, outside under both assignments. With raw HDI the means are -4.4 and 1.2 (main sign; within under the first assignment) and p 0.625. Mouse 8's square value (48 degrees) rests on 2 cells. Changed from partially reproduced after verification.
deviations: The sign of the change in preferred direction is not stated in the paper. Taken as the earlier session minus the later one (assumption), the convention under which the per-mouse means of Fig. 1g (change of each session relative to the last) have the paper's sign in 5 of 5 mice; here it is the first visit minus the later one. Both signs are shown.

outcomes.statement: Per animal of the single-visit protocol, the circular mean change in preferred direction relative to the first visit was 4.7, -0.4, -15.5, 5.4 and -6.2 degrees.
outcomes.source: Extended Data Fig. 10b legend
outcomes.quote: Circular mean ± s.d. per animal with pooled environments in degrees... 4.7 ± 3.4, −0.4 ± 5.8, −15.5 ± 34.7, 5.4 ± 10.8, −6.2 ± 10.9
outcomes.notes: Circular means over the five later sessions of each mouse (both environments pooled), with the change taken as the first visit minus the later one (main sign reading); all 5 within tolerance and all with the paper's sign. With raw HDI also 5 of 5 (5.27, -4.86, -12.03, 7.31, -8.29). With the opposite sign (later minus first, the sign before verification) 3 of 5 are within tolerance (2 of 5 with raw HDI), where the criterion asks for 4. Changed from not reproduced after verification.
deviations: Sign of the change as for edf10c-environment-identity (assumption); the outcome changes with it.

findings.statement: The tuning_curves table (processing/ophys/tuning_curves) of every imaging file holds one curve repeated for every ROI. In 401 of 402 sessions it is the curve of ROI 0, smoothed with a kernel of about 4 bins (median correlation 0.995). The table's description says it holds the tuning curve of each ROI.

Each protocol's files carry a CellReg table for that protocol only, and nothing links ROIs across protocols. The probe trials of Fig. 3 (the first week of the protocol "4 environments are visited weekly in a random order, for 4 weeks") cannot be matched to the last visits of the two-week protocol, so Fig. 3 cannot be tested. A cross-protocol registration table would fix this.
The electrophysiology files hold spike times and electrode groups only, with no waveforms; the waveform features of Extended Data Fig. 7f-h cannot be computed.

The probe week of Fig. 3 is not labelled as such. It is the first week of the random-order protocol, whose description (four weeks of random visits) also covers the three weeks of Extended Data Fig. 9, where the paper describes a week of probe trials followed by four further weeks.

The dandiset holds 402 imaging sessions (367 for mice 1 to 5) where the paper reports 388, and random-order sessions of mouse 5, whose field of view the paper says was lost before the probe trials. Sessions last 902 to 1799 s where the Methods state 20 min. The circular protocol has 19, 20, 19, 19 and 20 sessions, as Extended Data Fig. 1e states.

Each electrophysiology file holds two explorations of each of the three environments, separated by sleep, where the paper describes one. The files hold 347 units, 254 of them on PoSub shanks (the paper's n of 254 cells) and the rest in cortex or CA1.

The CellReg scores (scratch/Cell registration scores) include values below 0, 102 of 5,190 rows over all protocols and mice, down to -1.24, which a CellReg confidence score (0 to 1) cannot take. The files do not describe the score.
The dandiset's related publication and each file's related_publications point to the bioRxiv preprint (10.1101/2024.06.13.598909), not the Nature article.

Questions for the authors on the HD cell rule. Is the HDI computed on the raw or the smoothed tuning curve, and is the kernel 12 degrees or 12 bins? Smoothed HDI with a 12 degree kernel reproduces the paper's session and pair counts here, but raw HDI gives about twice as many HD cells, the outcomes of edf2ab-jaccard, fig2h-coherent-remapping and edf4c-previous-session change with it, and part of fig1f-example-stable (no mouse with 18 sessions matches) and of edf4ij-pv-decay (mouse 5's mean at the longest interval is 0 or below) fails with it. Is "detected in at least six sessions" registered by CellReg or HD in those sessions, and which sessions enter the average HDI? With either HDI the proportions of Extended Data Fig. 1e are not reproduced (main reading 0.12, 0.40, 0.04, 0.29, 0.07).

Questions for the authors on pairwise offsets and drift rates. Are angular offsets unsigned (0 to 180 degrees)? The paper's shuffle medians (51 to 57) match unsigned offsets (expected 52.7), while signed offsets give 90; unsigned was assumed. How is the drift rate per week computed? A least-squares slope against day difference was assumed; a line through the origin gives two to three times larger rates. What is the sign of a change in preferred direction? Taken as the earlier session minus the later one, the paper's signs of Fig. 1g and of Extended Data Fig. 10b are both matched (5 of 5 each), and Extended Data Fig. 10b,c are reproduced; with the opposite sign they are not.

Questions for the authors on the decoders. What are the XGBoost hyperparameters, how is dF/F normalized, how is population activity summed for the top 50% bins, do cells have to be HD cells in the test session, and is the error variance of Extended Data Fig. 8c circular or linear? Library defaults, division by the maximum, the sum, HD in both sessions and both variances were used; the circular variance matches the paper's values and the linear one does not. Requiring test cells only to be registered in the test session gives the same outcomes.

verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The first executed notebooks with the conclusion cells and the summaries removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier checked the archive for the blocked claims and tested helper functions on synthetic inputs. Its report had no attempt record and gave its own outcome for each claim; 26 of 32 agree with the record as handed over.

disagreements.reason: Under 12deg/raw, reading (a), 5 of 5 mice keep at least 80% of the 1-day index. Under the main reading only 2 of 5 (reading a) or 3 of 5 (reading b) do.

Both absence tests are non-significant under every configuration. Displacement against score is significant only under pooled raw HDI with x3 correction (p 0.0416); it would be 0.056 with four tests, and the main reading gives 0.50. n is 28 or 56, against 72. The analysis keeps only cells with CellReg score above 0.8, while the paper tests "all cells" (n = 72) and separately "cells with CellReg score over 0.8"; the correction is over 3 tests where the claims file lists 4.
No configuration meets both parts. Under the main reading medians are 3 of 5 within tolerance but mouse 3 has p 0.079. Under 12deg/raw all p below 0.05 but medians are 2 of 5.

All V-tests are significant. V is within tolerance for week 2 and week 4 but not week 3. The drift rate misses 1.6 +- 0.16 under every reading. "Reduced retention" needs the blocked fig3de. "The random protocol's first week is the probe week" is stated without an output. Run only under the main reading.

Reproduced under the sign reading not run. As run, square is -12.8, outside tolerance under both assignments by 0.3 degrees. The sign of the change in preferred direction is never run both ways; the Methods do not fix the cross-correlation direction. Negating the printed means puts both within tolerance under the first assignment. The Wilcoxon is non-significant either way.

Reproduced under the sign reading not run. As run, 3 of 5 are within tolerance. Negated, the means are 3.25, -3.07, -12.43, 4.68, -7.71 against 4.7, -0.4, -15.5, 5.4, -6.2, all 5 within tolerance with every sign matching.

verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebooks of the round-1 revision, with conclusions and summaries, the attempt record, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier agreed with all 32 outcomes and found no place where the claims file misreads the paper. It also reported that the README run time (25 minutes, against 40.7 printed) and main cell 2 (16 minutes, against 1992 s printed) were stale; both now refer to the printed times or to recent runs.

entries.name: skromne-carrasco-2026
entries.title: Months-long stability of the head-direction system (Skromne Carrasco et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Skromne Carrasco, Viejo and Peyrache (2026) on dandiset 001676, which holds 402 Miniscope sessions of postsubiculum HD cells in ten mice over four protocols and one silicon probe session in each of four mice. It tests the stability of preferred directions and pairwise offsets over four weeks and across four environments, the environment code, remapping between environments, memory after a single visit, and the electrophysiology offsets. The probe trials of Fig. 3 cannot be linked to earlier sessions, and the spike waveforms are not in the files.
